missingColumnsPolicy: The 51 columns the datamodel declares but the production database lacks are all nullable or defaulted (verified by scripts/pg/drift-report.mjs, which reports zero required-without-default columns over existing rows). The importer simply omits them and Postgres applies the default.

Job.invoiceNumber.finding: 13 invoice numbers appear on more than one Job (15 surplus rows). Production has no Job_invoiceNumber_key index, so the duplicates were never rejected. The job numbers involved come from different months (EIS-4/2026/0020, EIS-5/2026/0020, EI-2026-0020), which points at a document-numbering sequence collision rather than genuine duplicate invoicing.
Job.invoiceNumber.resolution: Job.invoiceNumber is a denormalised copy; the Invoice table is authoritative and its own invoiceNumber values are unique with no duplicates. For each duplicated number there is exactly one Invoice row and it references exactly one Job. Keep the value on that job; set it to NULL on the others. No Invoice, Payment or Receipt row is touched.

DocumentBrandingSettings.orgId.finding: Two branding rows carry orgId=org_eis_01: the legacy id='singleton' row (updated 2026-04-11) and the per-org id='org_eis_01' row (updated 2026-06-06).
DocumentBrandingSettings.orgId.resolution: Keep orgId on the per-org row, which is authoritative and newer. Set orgId to NULL on the legacy singleton, which keeps it readable as the fallback that lib/document-branding.ts still looks for by id.

Job.why: 15 surplus duplicates cleared by the job-invoice-number resolver; invoiceNumber is not numeric so no sum is affected

DocumentBrandingSettings.why: legacy singleton's orgId cleared by the branding-singleton resolver

Receipt.why: orphaned payment ids nulled by the nullOrphan policy — see orphanPolicy

Receipt.paymentId.finding: Two receipts point at a Payment.id that is not in the dump: EIS/RCT/2026/0029 (UGX 650,000) and EIS/RCT/2026/0030 (UGX 450,000). Both are already voided, both carry voidReason "Payment deleted", and both were voided within 40 minutes of being issued on 2026-08-30. The payments were deleted in the application; SQLite enforced no foreign keys, so the dangling id string stayed behind.
Receipt.paymentId.decision: Null Receipt.paymentId on those two rows. The datamodel declares the relation onDelete: SetNull with a nullable column, so this is not a repair but a replay: had the delete gone through Postgres, the database would have nulled the column itself. Nothing is lost — the receipt, its number, amount, invoice link, issuer, void reason and void timestamp all import unchanged, and the void reason already records where the payment went.
Receipt.paymentId.rejected: Skipping the two receipt rows. They are real issued-then-voided documents inside a numbered sequence; dropping them would leave two gaps in EIS/RCT/2026 that nothing explains.
